name: Cosine similarity
definition: The cosine of the angle between two nonzero vectors: their dot product divided by the product of their Euclidean norms. It is 1 for vectors that point the same way, 0 for orthogonal vectors, and -1 for opposite vectors, and it doesn't change when either vector is scaled by a positive number.
citations: Christopher D. Manning, Prabhakar Raghavan, and Hinrich Schütze, Introduction to Information Retrieval, Cambridge University Press, 2008, section 6.3.1.
Pang-Ning Tan, Michael Steinbach, and Vipin Kumar, Introduction to Data Mining, Addison-Wesley, 2006, section 2.4.5.

properties.says: Vectors 45 degrees apart have similarity cos(45°) = 0.7071.
A vector and a positive multiple of it have similarity 1.
A vector and its negation have similarity -1.
Swapping the arguments doesn't change the result.
Scaling one vector by 10 doesn't change the result.

provenance.why: Fable 5.1's passing runs confirmed this method with checks derived from its definition. Issue #9653 names it as a starting entry.
